scope_label: routine variation inherent in a process as it currently operates
definition: Common-cause variation is the ongoing variation produced by the recurring influences within a process as it currently operates.
explanation: When those influences remain sufficiently stable, results vary within a pattern that can be estimated from process data. A single high or low result within that pattern does not by itself identify a new cause.
Reducing this variation generally requires changing the process or its conditions, rather than reacting separately to each observation.
